dedupe_keys.name: louisiana department of health simulation of hurricane air evacuation of hospital patients simul8 case study

description: This case study describes how the Louisiana Department of Health tested its plans for evacuating hospital patients by air before hurricanes and tropical storms, when in-state surge capacity and ambulance capacity are insufficient and patients must be flown to neighbouring states. The vendor Simul8 Corporation published it as a free customer case study available online, built with the department's emergency preparedness staff. The team first built a spreadsheet model: 12 to 18 hospitals possibly needing evacuation, 555 to 619 patients at 95 percent confidence, 54 medically configured jets carrying one patient each, two or three departure airfields, 50 ambulances per airfield and up to seven receiving airports in six states, with round trips of 1.5 to over 3 hours and at most five jets on the ground per airport. Simul8 consultants then built a visual discrete event simulation adding flight cancellations, breakdowns and maintenance, patient types and loading rates within a 38-hour window. Coverage is Louisiana. Caveats: it is vendor marketing material, the model is not public, and results beyond the scenarios described are not reported. Outcomes reported are a model that staff can modify, scenario runs such as 600 patients from 12 hospitals, and over 80 hours saved compared with spreadsheets. Simulation uses: an example of discrete event simulation for emergency response and evacuation capacity planning of hospitals. Related records: the Hurricane Sandy hospital evacuations study (case_study-hurricane-sandy-nyc-hospital-evacuations) and the Stockholm evacuation exercises (case_study-region-stockholm-hospital-evacuation-simulation-exercises) are comparable.
